patient_overview.name: Brooks Little
patient_overview.description:
Brooks Little is a 43-year-old warehouse-shift forklift operator working part-time, living in East Orange with his wife, kids, and in-laws in a crowded household of seven. He comes to the visit for a routine check tied to his BMI but makes it clear he thinks the whole thing is a formality, launching into long tangents about his job, his truck, and articles he's read online rather than answering directly. He's proud of being the kind of guy who 'figures things out himself' and bristles at anything that sounds like being told what to do, though underneath the bravado there are real money pressures shaping what ends up in his stomach.</description>

demographics.occupation: Part-time forklift operator at a regional warehouse distribution center
demographics.residence: East Orange, New Jersey; household of 7
demographics.cultural_context: Brooks grew up in a working-class East Orange household where meals were whatever stretched furthest, and he carried that practical, no-frills attitude toward food into adulthood. He values self-sufficiency and being the one who 'figures it out' rather than asking for help, a trait reinforced by years of hourly warehouse work and now a crowded multigenerational household he feels responsible for provisioning. Food, to him, is fuel to get through a long shift, not something to fuss over, and he's wary of outside advice that doesn't account for the real cost of groceries on a tight budget.
